content: Unfortunately, $\mathit {PMI}(w,c)$ goes to negative infinity when the word-context pair $(w,c)$ does not appear in the training corpus. Due to unreliable statistics, this happens very frequently in finite corpora. Many models work around this issue by clipping negative $\mathit {PMI}$ values at 0, a measure known as Positive $\mathit {PMI}$ ($\mathit {PPMI}$), which works very well in practice. An unanswered question is: “What is lost/gained by collapsing the negative $\mathit {PMI}$ spectrum to 0?”. Understanding which type of information is captured by $\mathit {\texttt {-}PMI}$ can help in tailoring models for optimal performance.
